title: Randomized Medicaid access reduces financial exposure and expands care use while health and work outcomes separate
source_unit: Low-income uninsured Oregon adults selected or not selected by Medicaid lottery

observations.period: 2008 lottery; first-year coverage and care-use follow-up

denominator.unit: randomized lottery treatment-control contrasts; published estimates

observations.method: Random assignment by lottery among low-income uninsured adults on an Oregon Medicaid waiting list; lottery selection instruments coverage and compares treatment and control outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: Local population and historical Oregon program; first-year effects do not identify a particular bill, care-forgoing episode, or current national Medicaid effect.
observations.subgroup: Uninsured low-income Oregon adults eligible for the lottery opportunity.
observations.counterinterpretation: More care use can reflect previously unmet need and does not by itself prove improved objective health.

denominator.unit: randomized lottery treatment-control contrasts; published estimates

observations.method: Lottery-based randomized coverage opportunity linked to surveys and commercial credit reports.
observations.uncertainty: Financial outcomes are study-specific and do not reveal the original care decision, household time substitution, or plan design outside the experiment.
observations.subgroup: Lottery-selected versus non-selected low-income uninsured adults.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower measured out-of-pocket exposure can coexist with premiums, taxes, provider access limits, or unmeasured time costs.

denominator.unit: randomized lottery treatment-control clinical and survey contrasts; published estimates

good_to_excellent_self_reported_health.unit: randomized treatment result; approximately 25 percent relative increase

objective_physical_health_effect.value: no statistically significant improvement detected across reported measures

observations.method: Lottery random assignment with approximately two-year survey and clinical follow-up including depression, self-reported health, blood pressure, cholesterol, glycated hemoglobin, and cardiovascular risk.
observations.uncertainty: Null objective-health results do not rule out longer-term or heterogeneous effects; self-reported outcomes and clinical measures are distinct.
observations.counterinterpretation: Coverage can improve access and mental-health security without changing every objective biomarker within the follow-up window.

denominator.unit: randomized lottery treatment-control labor-market contrasts; published result

observations.method: Oregon Medicaid lottery treatment-control comparison using administrative and survey outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: A labor null does not identify job quality, schedule control, caregiving, job lock, or household time response.
observations.counterinterpretation: Coverage can reduce financial exposure without changing employment status or earnings in the observed window.

boundary: The Oregon lottery identifies selected coverage effects for a historical low-income uninsured population; it does not complete the same-person bill-to-care-choice-to-household-adaptation-to-trust chain.
